title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector assistance to support vulnerable communities in drought affected areas in God-God and Moyale woredas, Somali region.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspangtThis integrated multi-sector response will be implemented by NCA in partnership with Pastoralist concern (PC) in close collaboration with key government sectors to support vulnerable communities in drought affected areas in God- God and Moyale woredas of Somali region. Both NCA PC have strong presence in Ader and Dawa zones, are in the right position to respond for prevent further deterioration of food security, water supplies sanitation, rebuilding of essential livelihoods addressing the protection needs of affected communities in a multisectoral approach. Number of intended targets for this project are 31,000 people. In this project NCA will fully be responsible for overall management of the project, build capacity of partners, provide close monitoring, manage purchase and transportation of project inputs, drilled shallow wells, manage coordination platforms, ensure quality and CHS standards, compile and share reports. PC is responsible in implementing planned activities at ground level in consultation with community and local officials. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will have 10 months lifespan, starting from August 15, 2023. The target communities of the proposed project include the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees host community affected by drought in God-God Moyale woredas. The project covers Agriculture, WASH Protection sectors with a total budget of $ 1000,002.87, of which 45 % is allocated for Agriculture and multipurpose cash, 31 % for WASH, and 24 % for protection. lt/spangtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will provide supplementary animal feed to 400 pastoralist and agropastoral farmers to subsidize their livelihood recovery, will provide training on DRR, procure 1000 breeding shoats from local market and distribute to 200 households who lost their animals as a result of drought, the project will provide animal vaccination de-worming support for 3000 small ruminants. During shoat distribution 1000 more households living in the same localities will be supported with vaccination. The project will procure distribute animal health kits for the CAHWs,lt/spangtltspangt lt/spangtltspangtprovide Voucher Based Animal Health Treatment for 350 heads of animalslt/spangtltspangt.lt/spangtltspangt The project will provide multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) to 906 households to enable them to prioritize and cover their acute needs in flexible manner. NCA and partner will follow SCWG guidance and the endorsed minimum expenditure basket (MEB), while doing MPCA. Thus, select beneficiaries will receive USD$ 141/person/round for one round. Targeted individuals will be selected based on clear criteria scoring system, including consideration of socioeconomic vulnerabilities. Criteria will especially consider families with monthly incomes that are below the poverty line, unemployed heads of households and vulnerable female headed households. To ensure continuation of the ‘red thread’ in programming, priority will further be given to GBV-affected individuals.lt/spangtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will create access to safe drinking water through scheme rehabilitation, provide training for HEW and community volunteers and hygiene promoters on recommended WASH practices, develop WASH SBCC materials for key message dissemination, construct four semi-permanent communal latrines with four stances each, provide WASH NFI for 800 HHs to respond to beneficiary’s immediate WASH services and will provide household water treatment chemicals for 800 HHs and HTH Chlorine (70% chlorine powder) for woreda Water office.lt/spangtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will conduct GBV sensitization and awareness raising, conduct protection mainstreaming and safety risk monitoring, identify, register, and provide cash for 2lt/spangtltspangt00 unaccompanied /separated children (UASC), PWDlt/spangtltspangt and GBV survivors/women lt/spangtltspangtgirlslt/spangtltspangt at risk with a rate of 141 USD/HHlt/spangtltspangt to access medical psychosocial care in collaboration with core actors, conduct capacity building trainings on basic GBV, GBViE, PSEA, and CBFM for partner, staffs beneficiaries, facilitate referral for 100 GBV survivors for immediate health and safety services. lt/spangtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
